prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1277; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a sideswipe that occurred while changing lanes. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 2: Photos from the scene, witness statements, and the other driver's account all describe the collision the same way. The other vehicle moved into the insured's lane as the insured was merging.

Entry 3: The damage to the right side of the insured vehicle lines up with the impact described, and there is no record of earlier damage to that vehicle.

Entry 4: The claimant reports a knee injury and is represented by counsel. Counsel has asked that all contact be routed through their office.

Entry 5: Police and witnesses confirm the claimant was riding in the insured vehicle at the time. The initial medical report describes a knee injury that fits the kind and force of the collision well.

Entry 6: No prior injury to the same knee appears in the records obtained so far. The claimant's account in the recorded statement and the later interview is consistent, although some small details were added in the later interview without changing the core account.

Entry 7: Treatment has continued to expand well beyond what this type of knee injury usually requires, with more visits and new services added month after month. An independent medical review has been requested to assess the treatment plan.

Entry 8: The file is under review pending the independent medical review and receipt of the remaining treatment records. The accident mechanics, vehicle damage, and occupant information are all consistent with the claim as reported.
